questions.q: What does "cluster" mean in the PostgreSQL sense, per this lesson?
options: One server's collection of databases, created by initdb — not a failover cluster
A group of physically separate PostgreSQL servers configured for high availability
A synonym for a single table's partitions
A Docker Swarm or Kubernetes deployment of PostgreSQL
questions.explain: PostgreSQL overloads the word "cluster" to mean one server's data directory and its collection of databases, distinct from a failover cluster.

questions.q: What does initdb actually create, per this lesson?
options: A new data directory with system catalogs, default databases, the WAL directory, and default configuration files
Only the postgres superuser password
A Docker image from scratch
A pg_hba.conf file with no other content
questions.explain: initdb creates the full cluster data directory: system catalogs, postgres/template0/template1 databases, WAL directory, and default postgresql.conf and pg_hba.conf.

questions.q: What are the two common real installation paths described in this lesson?
options: An OS package manager (like apt or Homebrew) and Docker's official postgres image
Compiling from source only, with no other supported method
A GUI installer wizard exclusive to Windows
Cloud-only managed services with no self-hosted option
questions.explain: The lesson describes OS package managers and Docker's official postgres image as the two common, legitimate ways to get a real PostgreSQL server running.

questions.q: According to the ordered install flow in this lesson, what should happen before opening up pg_hba.conf for real remote connections?
options: The binaries should be installed, initdb should create the cluster, the postmaster should be running, and the superuser password should be set
Nothing — pg_hba.conf should always be configured first, before installing any binaries
The server should be uninstalled and reinstalled
All client applications should already be deployed to production
questions.explain: The lesson's ordered flow places installing binaries, running initdb, starting the postmaster, and setting a real superuser password before adjusting pg_hba.conf for real connections.

questions.q: Why does the Docker official postgres image run initdb automatically, per this lesson?
options: It runs initdb on first launch if the data directory is empty, then starts the server
It never runs initdb — the user must always run it manually inside the container
It replaces initdb with a completely different, undocumented process
Docker does not support running PostgreSQL as a container at all
questions.explain: The official postgres Docker image automates initdb on first launch when the data directory is empty, which is why it's a common way to spin up a lab instance quickly.
